exceptiondispatchinfo-preserve-stack.title: Preserve exception stacks with ExceptionDispatchInfo
exceptiondispatchinfo-preserve-stack.short: Rethrow captured exceptions without replacing their original stack
exceptiondispatchinfo-preserve-stack.summary: ExceptionDispatchInfo captures an exception together with dispatch information so it can be thrown later while preserving useful origin details.
exceptiondispatchinfo-preserve-stack.why: Throwing a previously captured exception object directly can make diagnostics point at the rethrow site instead of preserving the original failure path.
exceptiondispatchinfo-preserve-stack.tips: Use normal throw inside a catch when possible; use ExceptionDispatchInfo when an exception must cross an asynchronous, queued, or callback boundary.

unmanagedcallersonly-reverse-pinvoke.title: Expose managed entry points to native code with UnmanagedCallersOnly
unmanagedcallersonly-reverse-pinvoke.short: Define reverse interop without creating a managed delegate
unmanagedcallersonly-reverse-pinvoke.summary: UnmanagedCallersOnly marks static methods that native code can call through an unmanaged function pointer under the attribute's restrictions.
unmanagedcallersonly-reverse-pinvoke.why: Treating arbitrary managed methods as stable native callbacks ignores calling conventions, lifetime, and runtime transition requirements.
unmanagedcallersonly-reverse-pinvoke.tips: Keep signatures blittable where practical, choose calling conventions deliberately, and do not call attributed methods directly from managed code.

skiplocalsinit-definite-assignment-bound.title: Treat SkipLocalsInit as an unsafe initialization boundary
skiplocalsinit-definite-assignment-bound.short: Skipping zero initialization requires stronger write-before-read discipline
skiplocalsinit-definite-assignment-bound.summary: SkipLocalsInit can suppress zero initialization for eligible stack locals, reducing work in specialized hot paths while weakening a safety assumption.
skiplocalsinit-definite-assignment-bound.why: Unsafe or stack-based code that reads bytes before explicitly writing them can observe unspecified prior contents.
skiplocalsinit-definite-assignment-bound.tips: Use only after measurement, keep affected methods small, and prove every byte is initialized before it is read or exposed.

environment-processpath-executable-locat.title: Use Environment.ProcessPath for the running executable path
environment-processpath-executable-locat.short: Ask the runtime for the current process executable location
environment-processpath-executable-locat.summary: Environment.ProcessPath reports the path used for the executable associated with the current process when the platform can provide it.
environment-processpath-executable-locat.why: Assembly locations and working directories describe different concepts and can be misleading in bundled or unusual deployment layouts.
environment-processpath-executable-locat.tips: Use ProcessPath only when the executable itself matters; use AppContext.BaseDirectory for application content rooted beside the app.

utf8jsonwriter-streaming-output-lifetime.title: Stream JSON output with explicit Utf8JsonWriter ownership
utf8jsonwriter-streaming-output-lifetime.short: Write UTF-8 JSON incrementally without building an object graph
utf8jsonwriter-streaming-output-lifetime.summary: Utf8JsonWriter emits JSON tokens directly to a stream or buffer, making output shape, flushing, and ownership explicit.
utf8jsonwriter-streaming-output-lifetime.why: Materializing a large intermediate object or string can add memory pressure when output can be produced sequentially.
utf8jsonwriter-streaming-output-lifetime.tips: Keep token nesting balanced, decide who owns the destination, and flush at meaningful boundaries rather than after every property.

timeprovider-timer-testability.title: Create testable timers through TimeProvider
timeprovider-timer-testability.short: Make timer scheduling use the same replaceable clock abstraction
timeprovider-timer-testability.summary: TimeProvider.CreateTimer lets code obtain timers from an injected time provider rather than binding scheduling directly to wall-clock runtime services.
timeprovider-timer-testability.why: Abstracting only current-time reads still leaves tests dependent on real waiting when timer creation bypasses the injected provider.
timeprovider-timer-testability.tips: Route both clock reads and timer creation through the same provider so tests can control temporal behavior consistently.

array-clear-reference-retention.title: Clear reusable reference arrays when retained objects matter
array-clear-reference-retention.short: Cached arrays can keep old object references alive
array-clear-reference-retention.summary: Arrays containing references keep those objects reachable until the slots are overwritten, cleared, or the array itself becomes unreachable.
array-clear-reference-retention.why: Returning a reference array to a long-lived cache without clearing it can extend the lifetime of an entire object graph unexpectedly.
array-clear-reference-retention.tips: Clear reference-containing buffers before long-term reuse when retention matters; avoid redundant clearing when the owner guarantees immediate complete overwrite.

iasyncenumerable-cancellation-propagatio.title: Propagate cancellation through IAsyncEnumerable consumption
iasyncenumerable-cancellation-propagatio.short: Cancellation must reach the asynchronous enumerator
iasyncenumerable-cancellation-propagatio.summary: WithCancellation supplies a CancellationToken to asynchronous enumeration so producers that support cancellation can stop pending work.
iasyncenumerable-cancellation-propagatio.why: Checking cancellation only around await foreach may leave the enumerator blocked in its own asynchronous operation.
iasyncenumerable-cancellation-propagatio.tips: Pass cancellation at the consumption boundary and ensure custom async iterators accept and honor EnumeratorCancellation where appropriate.

httpcontent-streaming-request-body.title: Stream large HTTP request bodies instead of pre-buffering them
httpcontent-streaming-request-body.short: Let HttpContent produce request bytes from a stream
httpcontent-streaming-request-body.summary: StreamContent can expose an existing stream as an HTTP request body so large payloads do not need to be copied into one in-memory byte array first.
httpcontent-streaming-request-body.why: Pre-buffering large uploads increases peak memory and delays transmission until the whole payload has been prepared.
httpcontent-streaming-request-body.tips: Define stream ownership, cancellation, retry behavior, and whether the source can be replayed before enabling automatic retries.

unity-object-null-native-lifetime.title: Respect Unity Object null semantics after native destruction
unity-object-null-native-lifetime.short: UnityEngine.Object equality reflects native object lifetime
unity-object-null-native-lifetime.summary: UnityEngine.Object overloads equality so a managed wrapper can compare equal to null after its native object has been destroyed.
unity-object-null-native-lifetime.why: Using reference-only null patterns can treat a destroyed Unity object wrapper as a live component and then fail when accessing it.
unity-object-null-native-lifetime.tips: Use Unity's documented null comparison semantics for UnityEngine.Object instances and avoid retaining destroyed wrappers unnecessarily.
